summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for her 20th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She reported feeling well with no neurological symptoms or systemic complaints. The chemotherapy was administered without complications, and she experienced excellent nausea control with fosaprepitant instead of her prior antiemetic. Urine alkalinization was maintained throughout, and her methotrexate level at 30 hours was 0.17 uM, indicating safe clearance. A brain MRI showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence, with only stable chronic changes. She remained stable neurologically and hematologically, with no signs of infection or thrombosis. Aspirin was held during admission and restarted at discharge, with heparin bridging for DVT prophylaxis. She was discharged home in stable condition with no need for post-discharge leucovorin or bicarbonate, continuing her regular medications including those for chronic pain, asthma, and depression.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
